answers.Set Your Scope: I am Operations Manager for a 40-branch retail bank in Botswana, responsible for branch back-office processing (account opening, KYC refresh, loan document checks). Sector: retail banking.
answers.Map Opportunity One: Use document AI to pre-check KYC refresh packs before they reach the central team. Cost of inaction: about 1,900 packs a month are rejected for missing documents, roughly 950 staff hours and BWP 180,000 a year in rework. Nobody has acted because KYC sits between Compliance and Operations and neither wants to own a model that touches regulated files.
answers.Map Opportunity Two: For the Credit team, an AI assistant that drafts the first credit memo from the loan application. Cost of inaction: memo drafting averages 3.5 hours per SME loan, about 600 loans a year, delaying decisions by four days. Nobody has acted because the Head of Credit fears auditors will question AI-written memos.
answers.Map Opportunity Three: Stretch, outside my remit: Marketing could use branch transaction patterns to predict which SME customers are about to leave. Cost of inaction: we lost 210 SME accounts last year, about BWP 2.1m in deposits. Nobody has acted because Marketing has no data access agreement with Operations.
answers.Choose the One You Would Stake Your Repu: Opportunity One. I own the back-office process end to end and the rework cost is already in my budget line, so I can run a pilot in five branches without anyone else's approval. The Compliance concern is real, so the pilot keeps a human checker on every flagged pack.
answers.AI pressure-test and AI Lens: I asked an AI assistant to list overlooked automation opportunities in branch back-office work; it surfaced the credit memo idea I had not considered. I used it to sanity-check the BWP 180,000 estimate, which it put lower until I added the overtime rate. It could not tell me why Compliance resists ownership: that political read is mine, from two steering meetings this year.

results.feedback: This is an exceptional submission that perfectly captures the intent of the Opportunity Map. The learner provided highly specific, quantified costs of inaction, such as the BWP 180,000 rework cost for KYC and the BWP 2.1m deposit loss for SME churn. The organizational insights—specifically the 'political read' on the Compliance vs. Operations deadlock and the Head of Credit's fear of auditors—show a high degree of professional maturity. The selection of Opportunity One is strategically sound because it leverages the learner's direct control over the budget and process, allowing for a low-friction pilot. The AI Lens section demonstrates a clear understanding of how to use AI as a collaborator for divergent thinking and cost validation while maintaining ownership of the human-centric political navigation.

This is an exceptional submission that perfectly captures the intent of the Opportunity Map. Your scope is clearly defined and sets a professional context in Botswana's retail banking sector. Each of the three opportunities is highly specific, moving beyond generic 'efficiency' to name the exact process and department involved. Your estimation of the cost of inaction is excellent—citing 950 staff hours and BWP 2.1m in lost deposits provides the exact kind of 'real numbers' that drive business cases. Most impressively, your political read on why these opportunities haven't been taken (Compliance/Ops ownership disputes and fear of auditors) shows true leadership maturity. Your AI pressure-test reflection is a highlight; you correctly identified that AI can help with technical cost-checks but cannot navigate the cultural 'steering meeting' dynamics that you, as a human leader, must manage. This is a model answer.

This is an excellent submission that meets all the criteria for a high-scoring Opportunity Map. You have provided specific, localized examples within the Botswana retail banking context, using concrete numbers (BWP 180,000, 950 hours, 210 accounts) to quantify the cost of inaction. Your political reading of why these opportunities have remained untapped—specifically the 'no-man's land' between Compliance and Operations and the audit fears in the Credit team—shows a high level of situational awareness. The choice to stake your reputation on Opportunity One is well-reasoned, focusing on your direct span of control and a pragmatic approach to risk mitigation. Your AI pressure-test demonstrates a sophisticated use of the tool for both brainstorming and financial validation while correctly identifying that human judgment is still required for navigating internal politics.
